newsitem.title: INDONESIA: S.Africa says it wants to learn from Indonesia.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa says it wants to learn from Indonesia.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela said on Monday he had come to Indonesia to learn from the Southeast Asian nation's socio-economic achievements.
Speaking at a state dinner, Mandela praised the vision and leadership of Indonesian President Suharto in raising living standards during his 30 years in power.

"You have changed your country from a major importer of food to one based on self-sufficiency. Your experience in this regard will be valuable to many countries in the developing world, not the least on our African continent," he said.
Mandela, who arrived in Jakarta on Monday for a four-day state visit to Indonesia focusing on economic links, said trade between the two countries had increased four-fold in the past four years.
"We in Southern Africa have been furiously laying down the foundations for effective participation in the global economics of the new millennium," Mandela said.
"The easing of exchange controls is but one measure of our economic programme designed to boost trade and investment," he said.
Suharto said both countries faced the same problems in trying to catch up with developed nations.
"With our economic resources and complementary potentials, our two countries can meet our own demands within the framework of mutually beneficial bilateral relations," he said.
Mandela will hold talks with Suharto on Tuesday before meeting Indonesian Chamber of Commerce members. He leaves for Bangkok on Wednesday.
The trip is Mandela's third visit to Indonesia since his release from prison in 1990, but the first state visit.
